parts.visual:
Ten years ago, you bought a software CD for $100 and owned it forever. Today, you pay $10 every month until you die. Welcome to SaaS (Software as a Service).

The Math of Subscriptions:
1. Recurring Revenue (MRR): The holy grail of modern business. You start every month knowing exactly how much money you will make.
2. Churn Rate: The percentage of customers who cancel their subscription each month.
3. Lifetime Value (LTV): How much total money a customer pays before they finally cancel.
parts.audio: SaaS (Software as a Service) replaced one-time purchases with monthly subscriptions. Wall Street loves the Subscription Economy because it creates highly predictable Monthly Recurring Revenue, as long as the company can control its Churn Rate.

questions.question: A CEO changes their software pricing from a 'One-Time $500 Purchase' to a '$50/Month Subscription'. In the first year, revenue drops. But five years later, the company is worth billions. Why?
options: Because of the Lifetime Value (LTV). Over 5 years, the customer pays $3,000 instead of $500, and Wall Street values 'Recurring Revenue' much higher than one-time sales.
questions.correct_answer: Because of the Lifetime Value (LTV). Over 5 years, the customer pays $3,000 instead of $500, and Wall Street values 'Recurring Revenue' much higher than one-time sales.
questions.explanation: This is exactly what Adobe did when they transitioned Photoshop from a CD to a Cloud Subscription. Their stock price exploded.

questions.question: Listen to the SaaS investor. What metric is he terrified of?
questions.tts_text: You are acquiring 10,000 new users a month, which is great. But your cancellation rate is 15% a month. You are pouring water into a bucket with a massive hole in the bottom.
options: The Churn Rate. High churn means the product is fundamentally broken, and the company will eventually collapse once it runs out of new people to acquire.
questions.correct_answer: The Churn Rate. High churn means the product is fundamentally broken, and the company will eventually collapse once it runs out of new people to acquire.
questions.explanation: In SaaS, fixing Churn is infinitely more important than acquiring new users.

questions.question: What is the psychological trick behind 'Auto-Renewal'?
options: It leverages human laziness (friction). Once a user enters their credit card, they will often keep paying for months or years simply because they forget to cancel or find the cancellation process too annoying.
It is required by the government.

questions.explanation: Many subscription businesses rely heavily on the 'Gym Membership' model—people pay, but they never actually go.

questions.question: What does 'MRR' stand for?
options: Monthly Recurring Revenue. The total predictable income a company expects to receive every single month from active subscriptions.
questions.correct_answer: Monthly Recurring Revenue. The total predictable income a company expects to receive every single month from active subscriptions.
questions.explanation: MRR is the heartbeat of any modern technology company.
